name: Container_Value_SetFromRef
signature: void Container_Value_SetFromRef(ContainerValue* value, u32* ref, u32 owner)
summary: Copies the value pointed to by ref into a stack temporary and hands it to Container_Value_Set, i.e. the 'assign from a reference' form of the container setter. All fourteen named callers are regex-VM op handlers, so the container is the regex operand/value container.
evidence: All 14 named callers are Regex_* op handlers (Regex_MatchSequence, Regex_OpPushValue, Regex_OpBuildOperandSets, Regex_OpCopySetNormalized, Regex_OpPushValueFromLeft ...), which pins the container to the regex operand stack; the body is a literal copy-then-set wrapper around Container_Value_Set, so the name needs no further qualification.

name: Gfx_Overlay_SubmitQuad
signature: void Gfx_Overlay_SubmitQuad(GfxOverlayState* state, GfxCmdBuf* cmdbuf, GfxNode** node, int* quadDesc, unsigned int limit)
summary: Emits the GPU state for one overlay quad: rewinds the command-buffer slot to its saved mark, writes the texture sampler config and the draw elements, sets up the screen projection and appends the quad through Gfx_Overlay_AddQuad. Called once per render element from Gfx_SubmitSortedElement, so it is a per-quad submit, not a batch begin.
evidence: Its only caller Gfx_SubmitSortedElement submits one render element and calls this next to Gfx_Overlay_AddQuad and Gfx_SubmitScreenQuad, so the 'BeginBatch' reading is wrong; the body rewinds the cmd slot, writes the sampler config and draw elements and ends by constructing the quad descriptor that Gfx_Overlay_AddQuad consumes.

name: Ui_ItemRef_ResolveCurrentItem
summary: Resolves the id reported by the window's owner object (vtable +0x48 then +0x84) as an item: fills the ItemRef at self+0x1754 through Item_LookupRecord and stores the secondary table entry from 0x0063DF9C at self+0x175C. Called from the text and party-status update paths, so it refreshes the item the window is showing.
evidence: Disassembly shows Item_LookupRecord(&self->f_1754, id) followed by self->f_175C = 0x0063DF9C(dm, id); no model or model handle appears anywhere, so 'ResolveModel' was wrong. The six callers are the text/party-status update paths (Text_TalkWindow_Update, Battle_ActionSequence_ConsumeItem, Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanelSequence, Ui_PartyStatusWindow_CommitRows).

name: Battle_Ui_ShowUnitsById400_360_361
summary: Shows the three special battle units (body ids 400, 0x360 and 0x361) in each of the four battle unit lists: binds each found unit to the battle scene, attaches its part resources and plays animation 0x36. The hide counterpart is 0x005A57B8.
evidence: The pair 0x005A55B8/0x005A57B8 differs only in the show/hide flag passed to 0x00603B6C (0 vs 1) and the animation id (0x36 vs 0x34), and both are called from Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanelSequence; the list at battle work +0x428C is the 4 x 0x1C unit table from FACTS.md, so these are show/hide, not fades.

name: Battle_Ui_HideUnitsById400_360_361
summary: Hides the three special battle units (body ids 400, 0x360 and 0x361) in each of the four battle unit lists: unbinds each found unit from the battle scene and plays animation 0x34. The show counterpart is 0x005A55B8.
evidence: Same unit lookups as 0x005A55B8 but with the hide flag 1 for 0x00603B6C and animation 0x34; both are called from Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanelSequence, so the pair is show/hide rather than fade in/out.

name: Battle_ActionCommand_SpawnSpeakerBalloon
summary: Battle action-sequence command handler: when the command carries a payload it resolves the acting party member, jitters a screen position from the member's f_9C/f_9E with the battle RNG, tops the member's HP back up and spawns the speaker balloon through Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnSpeakerBalloon, then frees the command object.
evidence: Callees are now named: Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnSpeakerBalloon, Actor_ReleaseAndFree, Game_GetWork, Os_GetGameWork, std_FastSinCos. The visible effect is spawning the balloon (the old 'SetSpeakerTextPos' described only the position maths), and the function always ends by freeing the command object, which is the action-command handler shape.

name: Battle_ActionCommand_PushSpeakerMessage
summary: Battle action-sequence command handler: queues a battle message for the acting unit - either the plain 8/0x19 message or, in 3D mode, after clearing the unit's f_34 and adding state flag 4, the 0x19 variant - through Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry. No balloon is spawned here.
evidence: The only message-producing callee is Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry (0x003FBE4C) and the body builds the {actor, 0, msgId, 0xFF.., 0xFFFF..} entry that FACTS.md identifies as a battle message; Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnSpeakerBalloon is not called, so 'ShowSpeakerPopup' overstated it.

name: Battle_ActionCommand_SetActorPoseAndPushMessage
signature: void Battle_ActionCommand_SetActorPoseAndPushMessage(BattleUiWindow* self, BattleUnit* unit, u32 pose)
summary: Battle action-sequence command handler: applies the command's actor state (clearing the previous one through vtable +0x50 when the new value is 0, then vtable +0x110) and queues the battle message whose id comes from self->f_175C->f_D6, marking self->f_17F9.
evidence: The body is two vtable calls on the command's actor plus one Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry; the message id is read from self->f_175C->f_D6, the same field the sibling handlers use, so this is a pose-plus-message command rather than a popup.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenChild_Ctor_77E254
summary: Constructor of one of the fifteen child objects built by 0x002ADD3C: chains Ui_MotionPath_Ctor, installs vtable 0x0077E254, clears about 0x38 state words and chains four 0x004B65C0 sub-objects. The vtable shares Camera_Field_Delete (+0x04) and Camera_Field_Update (+0x10) with the field-camera vtable 0x0077E258, so the object is camera-related, but the exact class is still unresolved.
evidence: New: the vtable it installs (0x0077E254) has Camera_Field_Delete at +0x04 and Camera_Field_Update at +0x10, i.e. the field-camera virtuals, while the only caller 0x002ADD3C is itself called from Field_InitSceneObjects and builds fifteen mixed scene children. That contradicts a pure 'UI screen child' but does not identify the class, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassA
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassA(u32 arg1, int arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Field2D scene render pass: dispatches the spatial grid, walks the 0xE0-byte object records and issues the direct and quad draws for each live object, then applies the per-object attributes. The Thumb entry has a lost prologue (unaff_r4/unaff_r11), so only the call set identifies it as a render pass.
evidence: Damaged Thumb body (unaff_r4, unaff_r11, in_stack_*): the prologue is lost, so the object pointer and the argument list are guesses. The call set (Field2D_SpatialGrid_DispatchRenderObjectsB, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectsDirect, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectQuads, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectBatch) only proves it is a Field2D render pass, not which one, so the chip/sprite split is dropped.

name: maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectPassB
summary: Field2D scene render pass, a strict subset of 0x005C6E12: dispatches the spatial grid, then walks the 0xE0-byte object records issuing the direct and quad draws, and finally the batch pass. The Thumb entry has a lost prologue (unaff_r4/unaff_r5), so only the call set identifies it.
evidence: Damaged Thumb body (unaff_r4, unaff_r5, unaff_r11, in_stack_*): the prologue is lost. Its call set is a subset of 0x005C6E12's, so the sprite-vs-chip split the old name claimed cannot be demonstrated; only 'a Field2D render pass' is supported.

name: Field2D_Sprite_UpdatePositionAndHash
signature: void Field2D_Sprite_UpdatePositionAndHash(Field2DSprite* self, int* arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Steps one moving 2D sprite: checks the chip transition, either advances the bob animation or moves the sprite to the new world position, then re-inserts it into the spatial hash and fires the sprite's update callback.
evidence: All seven callees are now named (Field2D_Sprite_CheckChipTransition, Field2D_Bob_UpdateLoop, Gfx_Actor_SetPositionXY, Game_SetTwoFlags, Ui_SpatialHash_Insert, Gfx_Trail_TryConnectCell, Ui_WidgetList_DispatchEvent) and the body is exactly 'transition check -> bob or move -> rehash -> callback', which is what the name says.

name: Gfx_Node_SetChildHandle
summary: Replaces the handle attached to a scene node at +0x168: detaches the old one (0x005E785C), stores the new handle and attaches it (0x005E7650). All five callers are sprite/animator creation paths that attach a freshly created object to a node.
evidence: The five named callers (Field_Actor_CreateSprite, Gfx_AddFColAnimator, Field_ModelObj_UpdateEffect, Field_MultiPart_CreateSpriteFromResource, Field_MultiPart_CreateSpriteFromResourceB) all create a sprite or animator and then attach it, which is exactly the detach/store/attach triple in the body.

name: Gfx_SceneSpritePool_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a resource-owning scene-sprite container: writes the incoming vtable, destroys the three 0x20-byte sub-objects and the three handles, releases every 0x20-byte scene sprite in the page array, then restores the base vtable 0x0077F6C4 on the shared base.

Nothing in the body, the vtable or the single caller (Ui_WorldMap_Setup) mentions fonts or glyphs, so 'Font_GlyphCache' was wrong.

name: maybe_HandleRecord_GetNameLength
summary: Returns the length of the wide name at rec+8 when the record's four leading id bytes are all set (none is 0xFF), and 0 otherwise. It is a validity-gated name-length getter, not an assert: nothing aborts.
evidence: 0x00100B74 is wcslen (Thumb loop counting u16 until 0, then bx lr - see asm/text/text_00100048.s), so the tail call returns a value instead of aborting; the four 0xFF comparisons are a 'record is initialised' test. The old 'Assert...Valid' name was wrong on both counts.

name: BattleAi_FindBestCandidate
summary: Scans the sixteen candidate pointers at self+0x9BD0 and returns the usable one (vtable +0x24 and +0x10 non-zero) with the highest vtable +0x94 score, or null when none qualifies.
evidence: Four of the five callers are BattleAi_* (BattleAi_FilterUsableCandidates, BattleAi_EvaluateTacticMixItUp, BattleAi_EvaluateTacticDontUseMp, maybe_Battle_SelectActionForMode) and the fifth, 0x00275E9C 'Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode7', lies inside the poisoned 0x00269F64..0x00277700 BattleAi range from FACTS.md - so this is the AI candidate scorer, not text layout.

name: BattleAi_HasCandidateCapacity
signature: u32 BattleAi_HasCandidateCapacity(BattleAiState* self, int required, int mode)
summary: Gate used before appending AI action candidates: when the actor carries neither of the special states 0x73 and 0xCB, mode 0 requires required == 0 and every other mode requires the actor's candidate count (vtable +0x98) to be at least required; returns 1 when the check is skipped or passes.

name: Party_Member_CountMatchingSkills
summary: Counts how many of the six skill ids stored at record+0x54..+0x59 the given party member has learned: for each of the six it walks the member's learned skills (Party_CountLearnedSkills / 0x006298D0) and tests them with SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill, then returns the number of hits.
evidence: The loop compares record+0x54..+0x59 against the member's learned skills via Party_CountLearnedSkills and SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill, and all three callers are skill-panel / past-place UI paths (Ui_SkillPanel_OnConfirm, Ui_SkillPanel_OnCursorMove, Ui_PastPlaceWindow_HandleInput) - so it counts matching skills, not animation 'parts'.

name: Field2D_SpriteBlock_UpdateChipRange
summary: Recomputes the map-chip span covered by a 2D sprite block: sets the block scale, starts the path movement of every 0xE8-stride line entry, converts the left and right edge (centre -2 / +2) into chip ids through Field2D_MapChip_PackLayerChipIds and reports the pair to the block's interface (vtable +0x24).
evidence: Nine named callers are all Field2D_* (Field2D_Step_WaitDistance, Field2D_Step_GetPosition, Field2D_Sprite_UpdateScreenBounds, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects, Field2D_Sprite_StepMove, Field2D_Sprite_CheckGimmickTrigger, Field2D_Scene_AllocLayerList) and every callee is Field2D map/sprite code, so the Field2D reading is settled; the 'TextWindow' parameter type in the old signature was a misnomer.

name: Spirit_CountRosterEntries
summary: Counts the leading valid entries of the fifty-entry spirit roster at savework+0x5FE4 (0x8C-byte records: wide name at +0, id at +0x88): the walk stops at the first entry whose name is 7+ characters, whose first character is 0, or whose id is -1, and returns how many were counted.
evidence: The disassembly is a loop over up to 0x32 records of 0x8C bytes at savework+0x5FE4 calling wcslen (0x00100B74) on each name and testing the id at +0x88 against -1; the real seed symbol GetSpiritNum (0x00149854) returns exactly this value, and Ui_ListData_BuildEntries uses it as the row count for the same 0x8C-stride records. The old 'ReleaseTailMember' name came from Ghidra truncating the body at the mis-marked-noreturn wcslen.

name: maybe_Ui_UpdateTouchFocus
summary: Damaged Thumb fragment: hit-tests a point against the row list (Ui_HitTestRows) and sets the focus flag of the hit row. The entry at 0x0015FA00 is a false function start inside the ARM routine at 0x0015F988, so the prototype and the argument list are guesses.
evidence: The body is full of unaff_r4/unaff_r7/unaff_r9/unaff_r11 and in_stack_* arguments, and the entry is a mid-function split of 0x0015F988, so nothing about the signature can be trusted; the hit-test plus focus-flag shape is all that is visible.

name: Actor_Action_Move_ApplyShadowHeightToActors
signature: void Actor_Action_Move_ApplyShadowHeightToActors(ActorActionMove* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Movement-action step: when the action mode is 1 or 2 and f_34 is not 1, it sets the actor's ground block (f_130 = 1, height at +0x12C from the current height minus f_9C, f_128 from 0x0029E488) and then copies the same height into every matching scene object's f_128/f_130.
evidence: The function is slot +0x10 of vtable 0x0075FCCC, whose other slots are Actor_Action_Move_DeletingDtor, _Setup, _Finish and _Update - so the Actor_Action_Move class prefix is confirmed by its own vtable, and the body's per-object f_128/f_130 height copy matches the name.

name: Field_ActorList_ForEachByType
summary: Actor-list operation: when the list's enable byte f_2E is set it plays the animation on the reference actor, builds the type filter and applies the same one-byte message to every actor of the matching type in the global scene-object list.
evidence: The function is slot +0x14 of vtable 0x007658FC, whose slot 0 is Field_ActorList_DeletingDtor and whose other slots are the two siblings in this batch - so the Field_ActorList class is confirmed by the vtable, not guessed.

name: Field_ActorList_ClearFlagByType
summary: Actor-list operation: initialises the filter state (f_2C from the reference actor's f_2E4, defaulting to 4, f_2E = 0, f_30 = 7, f_34 = 0) and clears byte +0x202 on every actor of the matching type in the global scene-object list.
evidence: Slot +0x04 of vtable 0x007658FC next to Field_ActorList_DeletingDtor (+0x00) and the two siblings in this batch, so the class is confirmed; the body writes 0 to object+0x202 for every type-matching actor.

name: Field_ActorList_SendMessageByType
summary: Actor-list operation: sends the one-byte message 1 to the reference actor and then to every actor of the matching type in the global scene-object list.
evidence: Slot +0x08 of vtable 0x007658FC next to Field_ActorList_DeletingDtor (+0x00) and the two siblings in this batch; the body builds a one-byte message and applies it to the reference actor plus every type-matching list entry.

name: maybe_Field_InitSharedParams
summary: One-time initialiser guarded by self->f_E4 == 0: allocates a 500-byte object, installs vtable 0x0075A7D4 and constructs a 19 x 24-byte array from 0x006C3354. The rest of the body is Ghidra absolute-address garbage (_DAT_00000020, 0x00726AA8->f_7C), so the 'shared params' reading is unproven.
evidence: The body is damaged: Ghidra turned the global copies into absolute addresses (_DAT_00000020, iRam000001ec), so the second half cannot be read. What is certain is the 500-byte allocation, vtable 0x0075A7D4 and the 19 x 24-byte std_ConstructArray; the single caller 0x00206408 is itself a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemDetail_Setup
summary: Fills the detail pane of an action window: sets message argument 5 from the selected entry (self->f_3570->f_51C), installs the format string through the message-format singleton *0x007AC834, copies party member 0's stats and status block into a local buffer for argument 6, and finally shows the pane with Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim.
evidence: Callees are now named (Message_SetArg, Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim, Ui_ActionWindow_Setup, Game_GetWork, std_memcpy), which confirms the 'fill the detail labels then show the pane' reading, but the owning window class is still only the first-pass guess and there are no callers, so the maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_ListWindow_SetVisibleAndSetTextLayers
summary: Visibility override of a list window: calls Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self, visible) and then refreshes the twelve 0x10-byte text layers at +0x70 with Ui_TextLayer_SetText, using each layer's stored id and alpha.
evidence: Slot +0x18 of vtable 0x0075E2EC, whose +0x1C slot is Ui_ListWindow_InitRowsAndPager - so the class is a list window, not a generic 'Ui_Widget'; the body's 12-iteration Ui_TextLayer_SetText loop is what the name describes.

name: Ui_EquipmentListWindow_SetVisible
summary: Shared visibility override for the equipment-list window family: calls Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self, visible) and, only when becoming visible and the sub-object pointer at +0x54 is set, tail-calls the object's own vtable +0x60 (the refresh slot).
evidence: The same pointer sits at slot +0x18 of four vtables (0x00760820, 0x00765274, 0x0076B1DC, 0x0077AECC) that all share slot +0x1C = maybe_Ui_EquipmentListWindow_InitPanes_2, so this is the equipment-list family's shared override, not a shop window; the disassembly shows the +0x54 gate and the vtable +0x60 tail call.

evidence: Disassembly: Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self+0x1B8, 1) with a constant 1, then a list refresh, then an 8-byte copy from 0x00729298 into self+0x144 - and 0x00729298 holds Ui_JewelShopWindow_UpdateSelect, so the callback install names the class. The function is entry 0 of the handler table at 0x00729288, whose neighbours are page/select handlers.

name: Ui_SkillPanel_SetVisible

name: Ui_TwoColumnListWindow_SetVisible

name: maybe_Ui_Selector_SetVisible
summary: Visibility override of a selector window: calls Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self, visible) and, when becoming visible with the animation byte at +0x48 set, resolves the game work block and starts the window's open tween.

The pointer is slot +0x18 of two vtables (0x0075E4B8, 0x0075E544) whose +0x1C slots are maybe_Ui_SetOwnerAndDispatch and Ui_LayoutChild_InitDispatch, so the generic Ui_Pane_ prefix is the honest one.

name: Ui_SevenSlotWindow_SetVisibleAndSetRowAlphas

name: Ui_NumberedTextWindow_SetVisible

evidence: Slot +0x04 of vtable 0x0076D5DC is Ui_NumberedTextWindow_Dtor and slot +0x1C is Ui_NumberedTextWindow_InitPanes, so the class is the numbered-text window, not a bare 'Ui_Pane'.

name: Ui_PagedIconSelectWindow_SetVisible

evidence: Slot +0x04 of vtable 0x00771920 is Ui_TextWindow_DeletingDtor and slot +0x1C is Ui_PagedIconSelectWindow_InitPanes, so the class is the paged icon-select window, not a generic 'Ui_Widget'.

name: Ui_PartyListWindow_SetVisible
summary: Visibility override of the party-list window: calls Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim(self, visible) and then refreshes the window's list.

name: Field_ActorAction_CreateRun
summary: Creates the run/walk movement action: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, installs vtable 0x0075A590 and the sub-object vtable 0x00782524, copies the literals 'Run' and 'Walk' into the two name buffers and sets state byte +0x17 to 1.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateCut
summary: Factory for one field-action class: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs vtable 0x0075959C, whose slots +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 are the three small overrides at 0x001BA290/0x001BA298/0x001BA294. The class is registered in the action table, but nothing in the body says which action it is.
evidence: The body is two stores (Actor_Action_InitDescriptor + vtable 0x0075959C) and the three override targets are unnamed, so 'Cut' remains the N_040 proposal only; the caller Actor_CreateActionTable confirms it is a table-registered action factory.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_CtorAlt
summary: Constructor of a second field-action class: allocates through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs vtable 0x0076AEEC, which differs from the base vtable 0x0076AE84 only in slot +0x10 (0x003E4008 instead of the base 0x00294BCC).
evidence: New: vtable 0x0076AEEC overrides slot +0x10 with 0x003E4008 while the base 0x0076AE84 keeps 0x00294BCC, so this is a real subclass - but 0x003E4008 is unnamed and the body is two stores, so the class name cannot be stated.

name: Actor_Action_BaseCtor
summary: Base constructor of the actor-action hierarchy: allocates the descriptor through Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs vtable 0x0076AE84, which keeps the base virtuals 0x00294BC8/0x00294BD0/0x00294BCC with no overrides.
evidence: Vtable 0x0076AE84 has no overrides at all (slots +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 are the base Actor_Action virtuals 0x00294BC8/0x00294BD0/0x00294BCC), and both callers chain it as a base - so it is the base Actor_Action constructor, not a field-specific one.

name: Ui_Object_SelectEmbeddedNode
summary: Broadcasts the selection flag to the children of the embedded node at self+0x3430: passes 1 only when that node equals the element pointer given in r1, so the node shows when it is the current selection and hides otherwise.
evidence: The body is a single tail call to the now-named Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(object+0x3430, object+0x3430 == arg2), the same shape as Ui_SelectElement 0x00259928 with +0x3430 instead of +0x838; the five callers are pane push/pop and bind paths that pass a node pointer.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_ReleaseChildrenB
summary: Child-list reset step (one of five near-identical copies): pops the child list down to the class minimum, re-links the embedded node at +0x1C4 and broadcasts visibility flag 1 to it. The copy is an entry of the handler table at 0x0072ADF4.
